title: Configuring ZDX alert rules: types, filters, metrics, throttling, delivery, templates and labels

prose.text: An alert rule is what raises a ZDX alert: it has a type, a severity, optional labels, criteria over metrics, filters, throttling and a delivery method; how a trigger and an alert's status behave is in [[zdx.alerts]]. {{rule-types}} The trigger article lists fewer types, and the two lists are set side by side in [[zdx.alerts]]. {{zdx-score-type-retired}} The help describes the ZDX Score type differently in places {{divergence:zdx-score-rule-type}}.

prose.label: Scope and filters.
prose.text: {{parameters-and-filters}} {{filters}} {{incident-types}} Which rules an admin can configure depends on scope: [[shared.admin-rbac.zdx:scope-covers-rule]].

prose.label: Throttling.
prose.text: {{throttling-device-groups}} {{throttling-call-quality}} {{throttling-network-intelligence}} The trigger article's throttling criteria are in [[zdx.alerts:throttling]]. Which meaning one throttling sentence has is open {{gap:incident-actions-sentence}}.

checks.do: Which rule type the alert belongs to, and whether the trigger article's shorter type list or the configuration article's longer one applies to the tenant's console.
Whether a rule still shows a ZDX Score type or was migrated, before treating the type as current.
For a rule that did not trigger, the type's throttling fields: repeat count, active devices, minimum devices or users impacted and the group they apply to.
For an alert that was not delivered, whether Muted is enabled and which delivery method the rule has.

rule-types.statement: The Configuring an Alert Rule article offers the types Applications, Call Quality, Device, Incident, Network, Network Intelligence and Real User Monitoring (RUM), and each rule has a severity of High, Medium or Low and optional labels.

quotes: Type: Choose from Applications, Call Quality, Device, Incident, Network, Network Intelligence, or Real User Monitoring (RUM).
Severity: Select High, Medium, or Low options for severity, depending on the impact of this event on users.
Labels (Optional): Select the applicable labels for the alert rule.

zdx-score-type-retired.statement: The Editing an Alert Rule article says the ZDX Score alert rule type is no longer recommended and any pre-existing ZDX Score rule has migrated to an Applications rule; for an existing ZDX Score rule an Applications or Network rule is created with ZDX Score selected as a criterion, and the throttling and other field values remain the same.

quotes: The ZDX Score alert rule type is no longer recommended for use. Any pre-existing ZDX Score alert rule type has migrated to an Applications alert rule type.
If you have an existing ZDX Score alert rule type, you must create an alert rule with the type as Applications or Network and then select ZDX Score as a criterion.
The throttling and other field values remain the same.

incident-types.statement: For an Incident rule one or more checkboxes can be selected from the Incident Type drop-down menu; if multiple incidents are selected, the criteria are predefined based on their minimum thresholds.

quotes: If you select Incident as your type, you can select one or more checkboxes from the Incident Type drop-down menu to configure an alert rule for. If you select multiple incidents, the criteria are predefined for you based on their minimum thresholds.

filters.statement: A rule's filter can include or exclude items but not both for the same filter, deleted or unknown users cannot be selected for the include and exclude criteria, and the limit for selected items in the Add Filter menu is 250 items.

quotes: You can select to include or exclude items from a filter, but you cannot choose to have both include and exclude for the same filter.
You cannot select deleted or unknown users for the include and exclude criteria.
The limitation for selected items in the Add Filter menu is 250 items.

parameters-and-filters.statement: By type, Applications rules choose a predefined or custom application and its Web probe; Call Quality rules a predefined UCaaS application; Network rules a predefined or custom application of the network type and its Cloud Path probe; RUM rules a predefined or custom application with RUM enabled; Device, Incident and Network Intelligence rules take filters only. Incident rules filter by geolocations, devices and users, Network Intelligence rules by Zero Trust Exchange, geolocations and ISPs, and the other types by geolocations, Zscaler locations, location groups, departments, user groups, users and devices.

quotes: | Applications | Application: Choose a predefined application or a custom application. Web Probe: Choose the Web probe for this application. | Geolocations Zscaler Locations Location Groups Departments User Groups Users Devices |

| Call Quality | Application: Choose a predefined application that is a Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS) application. | Geolocations Zscaler Locations Location Groups Departments User Groups Users Devices |
| Device | Filters only | Geolocations Zscaler Locations Location Groups Departments User Groups Users Devices |
| Incident | Filters only | Geolocations Devices Users |

| Network | Application: Choose a predefined application or custom application that is a network application type. Cloud Path Probe: Choose the Cloud Path probe for this application. | Geolocations Zscaler Locations Location Groups Departments User Groups Users Devices |
| Network Intelligence | Filters only | Zero Trust Exchange Geolocations ISPs |

| Real User Monitoring (RUM) | Application: Choose a predefined application or a custom application with RUM enabled. | Geolocations Zscaler Locations Location Groups Departments User Groups Users Devices |

metrics.statement: The criteria metrics the table lists include, for Applications, DNS Time, Page Fetch Time, Server Processing Time, Web Request Availability, ZDX Score, ZDX Score Drops and Zscaler Time to First Byte; for Call Quality, MOS and ZDX Score; for Network, Latency, Number of Hops, Packet Count, Packet Loss, ZDX Score and ZDX Score Drops; for Network Intelligence, Threshold Latency and Network Latency Deviation; and for Device the bandwidth, battery, CPU, disk, memory, received and sent bits and Wi-Fi Signal rows quoted in the article. Each incident type or subtype has a different minimum number of impacted devices.

quotes: | Applications | DNS Time Page Fetch Time Server Processing Time Web Request Availability ZDX Score ZDX Score Drops Zscaler Time to First Byte |
| Call Quality | MOS ZDX Score |

| Device | Bandwidth in mbps Battery Level CPU Idle CPU Kernel Usage CPU User Usage CPU Utilization Disk Reads in bps Disk Usage Disk Writes in bps Memory Usage Memory Used Received Bits in mbps Sent Bits in mbps Wi-Fi Signal |
| Network | Latency Number of Hops Packet Count Packet Loss ZDX Score ZDX Score Drops |
| Network Intelligence | Threshold Latency Network Latency Deviation |
Each incident type or subtype has a different minimum number of impacted devices.

criteria-logic.statement: Selecting All (and) triggers the alert if all thresholds are reached and Any (or) if any is; depending on the metric a criterion uses the <, >, <= or >= symbols with time in ms or percent, a ZDX Score criterion is chosen between 1 and 100, and for ZDX Score Drops the threshold sensitivity (for example high, medium, low) is based on a baseline score.

quotes: Select All (and) for the alert to trigger if all of these thresholds are reached. Select Any (or) for the alert to trigger if any of these thresholds are reached.

Depending on the metric, the criteria can use the <, >, <=, or >= symbols and the time (in ms) or percent (%) options to set up the criteria for your alert rule. For ZDX Score, choose between 1 and 100 for your alert rule.
For ZDX Score Drops, you can choose the threshold sensitivity (e.g., high, medium, low), which is based on a baseline score.

throttling-device-groups.statement: For Applications, Device, Network or Real User Monitoring (RUM) rules, throttling has Alert Only if Repeated (the number of times a triggering event occurs before an alert is sent; Zscaler recommends 3 or more), Minimum Devices Impacted (by Number or Percentage; alerts trigger even if only one device is present in a specific group and meets the criteria) and an In Group of Departments, Cities, Organization, Regions or Locations. In the article's example the alert does not trigger because there must be at least 5 active devices in Cairo.

evidence.after: Depending on the Alert Rule type selected, the Throttling options are:
quotes: Applications, Device, Network, or Real User Monitoring (RUM)
Alert Only if Repeated: Enter the number of times a triggering event occurs before an alert is sent. Zscaler recommends entering 3 or more.

Minimum Devices Impacted: Choose by Number or Percentage. The alert triggers only if this minimum number is reached. Alerts trigger even if only one device is present in a specific group and the device meets the alert criteria.
In Group: Select the groups these throttling options apply to: Departments, Cities, Organization, Regions, or Locations.
The alert won't trigger because there must be at least 5 active devices in Cairo.

throttling-call-quality.statement: Call Quality rules throttle by the number of impacted meetings in a 15-minute rolling time duration (within 1 and 10), the minimum number of total active participants in a meeting (within 3 and 10) and the number of impacted active participants (within 1 and 20) from a selected group (Department, Cities, Organization, Regions, Zscaler Locations).

quotes: Number of Meetings is: Enter the number of impacted meetings in a 15-minute rolling time duration within the range of 1 and 10.
Minimum Number of Active Participants is: Enter the number of total active participants in a meeting within the range of 3 and 10.

Number of Impacted Active Participants is: Enter the number of impacted active participants within the range of 1 and 20 from a selected group (Department, Cities, Organization, Regions, Zscaler Locations).

throttling-network-intelligence.statement: The throttling listed after the Call Quality options for Network Intelligence rules includes Alert Only if Repeated (Zscaler recommends entering 3 or more) and Minimum Users Impacted, which triggers the alert only if that minimum number of impacted users is reached.

quotes: Minimum Users Impacted: The alert triggers only if this minimum number of impacted users is reached.

evidence.after: Number of Impacted Active Participants is: Enter the number of impacted active participants within the range of 1 and 20 from a selected group (Department, Cities, Organization, Regions, Zscaler Locations).
quotes: Alert Only if Repeated: Enter the number of times a triggering event occurs before an alert is sent. Zscaler recommends entering 3 or more.

delivery.statement: If Muted is enabled no alerts are sent and the status of alerts can be viewed on the Alerts page; the delivery method otherwise is Email (an address, with an Email Preview of the email that will be sent) or a Webhook selected from previously configured webhooks or newly configured.

quotes: If Muted is enabled, no alerts are sent, and you can view the status of alerts on the Alerts page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Email: Enter the email address you want the alerts to be sent to. Click Email Preview to preview the email that will be sent.
Webhook: Set up a webhook to provide alerts. In the drop-down menu, select from previously configured webhooks or configure a new webhook.

rules-page.statement: The Rules page shows when each rule last triggered an alert and its Alert Delivery Method (Email or webhook if configured, empty if the rule is muted or none is configured), can be filtered by severity (High, Medium or Low) and can edit, mute, copy or delete a rule.

quotes: Last Triggered: The date and time that the rule last triggered an alert.
Alert Delivery Method: Email or webhook, if configured. If the rule is muted, or no alert delivery method has been configured, this field is empty.
Severities: You can filter for rules configured for High, Medium, or Low severity.
Edit, mute, copy, or delete a rule.

templates.statement: ZDX templates save frequently used alert rule criteria and can then prefill an alert rule when configuring a Zscaler Managed probe; a template's Type is Predefined or Custom and its Probe Type is Cloud Path or Web, and a predefined template cannot be edited or deleted but can be copied. Managing templates needs an admin role that supports Alerts and Configuration and a subscription level that supports Managed Monitoring.

quotes: You can create Digital Experience (ZDX) templates to save frequently used alert rule criteria. After saving a template, you can then use it to prefill an alert rule when you configure a Zscaler Managed probe.
Type: The template type is Predefined or Custom.
Probe Type: The probe type is Cloud Path or Web.
You cannot edit or delete a predefined template. You can copy the predefined template.
Your admin role supports Alerts and Configuration.
Your subscription level supports Managed Monitoring.

predefined-templates.statement: The predefined templates are Warning Availability (High, Web: Availability < 100% 2 times in 60 minutes across any 1 Zscaler Managed Location), Critical Page Fetch Time (High, Web: Page Fetch Time > 1000 ms 3 times in 15 minutes across any 2), Warning Page Fetch Time (Medium, Web: the same across any 1), Probe Failure (High, Web: Availability = 0% 3 times in 15 minutes across any 1), Critical Latency (High, Cloud Path: Latency > 5 ms 3 times in 15 minutes across any 2) and Warning Latency (Medium, Cloud Path: the same across any 1).

quotes: | Warning Availability | High | Web | Availability < 100% Occurs 2 times in 60 minutes Across any 1 Zscaler Managed Location |
| Critical Page Fetch Time | High | Web | Page Fetch Time > 1000 ms Occurs 3 times in 15 minutes Across any 2 Zscaler Managed Locations |
| Warning Page Fetch Time | Medium | Web | Page Fetch Time > 1000 ms Occurs 3 times in 15 minutes Across any 1 Zscaler Managed Location |
| Probe Failure | High | Web | Availability = 0% Occurs 3 times in 15 minutes Across any 1 Zscaler Managed Location |
| Critical Latency | High | Cloud Path | Latency > 5 ms Occurs 3 times in 15 minutes Across any 2 Zscaler Managed Locations |
| Warning Latency | Medium | Cloud Path | Latency > 5 ms Occurs 3 times in 15 minutes Across any 1 Zscaler Managed Location |

labels.statement: After a label is assigned to an alert rule it becomes part of the alert details and is seen in the delivered alert details when webhooks are configured; multiple labels can be applied to a rule for grouping, managing and assigning labels needs Full Alerts permission, and a label cannot be deleted if an alert rule is tagged with it. A new label's Name and Description can each be at most 120 alphanumeric characters including hyphen, space or underscore.

quotes: After assigning the label, the label becomes part of the alert details and is seen in the delivered alert details when you configure webhooks.
To manage and assign labels, you must have Full Alerts permission.
Create and apply multiple labels to an alert rule for grouping purposes.
You cannot delete a label if an alert rule is tagged with it.

evidence.after: In the Create New Label window:
quotes: The Name and Description can each consist of a maximum 120 alphanumeric characters including: hyphen (-), space ( ), or underscore (_).

zdx-score-rule-type.summary: Whether ZDX Score is still an alert rule type: About Rules still describes rules with Rule Type ZDX Score and the ServiceNow Mappings module maps a ZDX Score alert type, while Editing an Alert Rule says the type is no longer recommended and existing rules migrated to Applications.

quotes: Grouping ZDX Scores based on Departments, Cities, Organization, Region, or Zscaler Locations (specified Rule Type as ZDX Score).

positions.says: About Rules describes configuring a rule with Rule Type ZDX Score.

quotes: Mapping for the Zscaler alert type - ZDX Score: Provides mapping for all alerts that have been configured in Zscaler Admin Console as ZDX Score.

positions.says: The ServiceNow Mappings module maps alerts configured in the Admin Console as ZDX Score.

quotes: The ZDX Score alert rule type is no longer recommended for use. Any pre-existing ZDX Score alert rule type has migrated to an Applications alert rule type.

positions.says: The ZDX Score rule type is no longer recommended and existing ZDX Score rules migrated to Applications.

zdx-score-rule-type.impact: Whether a tenant can still create or see a ZDX Score rule type is unsettled; an alert reported as a ZDX Score alert may be an Applications or Network rule with a ZDX Score criterion.

incident-actions-sentence.title: What 'Only Incident Type alert rules can configure Actions' means
incident-actions-sentence.detail: Under Incident throttling the Configuring an Alert Rule article has a sentence saying only Incident Type alert rules can configure Actions; the capture does not say what Actions are in this context.
